findings.pdf_says: SORT Format 2 (table), COLLATING SEQUENCE clause. The printed figure is an outer BRACKET containing 'COLLATING SEQUENCE' followed by a BRACE with two alternatives:  alternative 1 = 'IS alphabet-name-1 [ alphabet-name-2 ]';  alternative 2 = an inner BRACE WITH CHOICE INDICATORS, i.e. a vertical bar just inside each side of the inner brace, spanning the two lines 'FOR ALPHANUMERIC IS alphabet-name-1' and 'FOR NATIONAL IS alphabet-name-2'. Rendered linearly:  [ COLLATING SEQUENCE { IS alphabet-name-1 [ alphabet-name-2 ]  |  { | FOR ALPHANUMERIC IS alphabet-name-1 | / | FOR NATIONAL IS alphabet-name-2 | } } ]
findings.why_it_matters: Two separate losses, both toward falsely-restrictive syntax. (1) The choice-indicator bars just inside the inner brace are gone; per 5.2.6.4 those bars mean the enclosed alternatives may each be specified at most once, in any order, so 'FOR ALPHANUMERIC IS alphabet-name-1' and 'FOR NATIONAL IS alphabet-name-2' may BOTH appear. Without the bars the markdown reads as select-exactly-one, making a legal table SORT that sets both an alphanumeric and a national collating sequence look illegal. (2) The nesting is garbled: 'IS alphabet-name-1 [ alphabet-name-2 ]' is shown inside the same inner brace as the two FOR lines, whereas the PDF makes it a sibling ALTERNATIVE to the whole bar-group. The identical construct in SORT Format 1 (page 775) has already been repaired in the markdown with box-drawing brackets plus a 'Figure notes (SORT Format 1)' paragraph; Format 2 was left unrepaired, so the two general formats of the same statement now contradict each other.
findings.suggested_repair:
Replace the Format 2 code fence with the same convention already used for Format 1 at page 775, e.g.

```
SORT data-name-2 ⎡ ON ⎧ ASCENDING  ⎫ KEY [ data-name-1 ] … ⎤ …
                 ⎣    ⎩ DESCENDING ⎭                       ⎦

    [ WITH DUPLICATES IN ORDER ]

⎡                      ⎧  IS alphabet-name-1 [ alphabet-name-2 ]     ⎫ ⎤
⎢ COLLATING SEQUENCE   ⎨ ⎧| FOR ALPHANUMERIC IS alphabet-name-1 |⎫   ⎬ ⎥
⎣                      ⎩ ⎩| FOR NATIONAL IS alphabet-name-2     |⎭   ⎭ ⎦
```

and add a 'Figure notes (SORT Format 2)' paragraph mirroring the one at page 775: the bar-group is a brace WITH choice indicators (5.2.6.4) so both FOR phrases may be specified in any order; it is one alternative of the enclosing brace, the other being the single-line 'IS alphabet-name-1 [ alphabet-name-2 ]' form; the whole COLLATING SEQUENCE clause is optional; required words underlined in the printed figure are SORT, ASCENDING, DESCENDING, DUPLICATES, SEQUENCE, ALPHANUMERIC, NATIONAL.

findings.pdf_says: 14.9.40.3   Syntax rules   (printed bold, the same heading style/level as 14.9.40.1 General, 14.9.40.2 General formats and 14.9.41.4 General rules)
findings.why_it_matters: A fourth-level clause is transcribed at markdown level 2, the same level as its own parent '## 14.9.40 SORT statement', so in the generated outline 14.9.40.3 becomes a sibling of 14.9.40 rather than a child of it. Its own siblings are inconsistent: 14.9.40.1 and 14.9.40.2 are '###', and every corresponding heading in the neighbouring START clause (14.9.41.1 through 14.9.41.4) is '###'. Section-navigation and any anchor/TOC generation built on heading depth mis-nest this clause.
findings.suggested_repair: Demote to '### 14.9.40.3 Syntax rules' to match 14.9.40.1, 14.9.40.2 and the whole 14.9.41.x subtree.

findings.pdf_says: 14.9.40.4   General rules   (printed bold, the same heading style/level as 14.9.41.4 General rules on page 785)
findings.why_it_matters: Same defect as 14.9.40.3: the clause is transcribed at markdown level 2, level with its parent '## 14.9.40 SORT statement', while the identically-ranked '### 14.9.41.4 General rules' (page 785) is level 3. The SORT clause's general rules therefore fall outside the SORT section in any outline built from heading depth.
